lens_summary: m9-74 closes the high finding m9-73 deferred, its visible symptom, and a medium one that the first fix uncovered. FIND-M9-73-CAS-PUT-ONE-WRITE-TRANSACTION-PER-EVENT: ContentStore::put opened a redb write transaction, inserted one row and committed, and redb's default immediate durability makes every commit a sync_data barrier, while SessionStore::save_session called put in a loop - one fsync per event, ~4.8 ms/event, so a 34,905-event crash session did not complete in 186 s against the sandbox client's 30 s tools/call timeout. The fix splits the pure encode step (bincode + LZ4 + BLAKE3) from the write, so a batch is fully encoded before any transaction opens and an encoding failure stores nothing, inserts a whole batch in one write transaction with the per-event dedup check preserved (a write transaction reads its own inserts, so duplicates inside a batch collapse too), and exposes put_many for save_session; put is now encode + insert_batch and keeps its hash. Evidence is a CountingBackend wrapping redb's real FileBackend that counts sync_data calls: a 500-event batch is asserted to stay under 4 barriers against a control loop of 50 puts that must issue at least 50, and save_session of 1,000 events is asserted to stay under 4 barriers and still round-trip. The backend is file-backed on purpose - an in-memory redb never syncs, so the assertion would pass for the wrong reason. FIND-M9-73-SESSION-EDGE-CASES-HEAVY-SAVE-NEVER-COMPLETES was the symptom row; with the batching in place the suite goes from 4 passed / 2 failed (never completing) to 6 passed / 0 failed in 65 s with the 30 s client timeout untouched, so the row was removed from AGENTS.md rather than reworded. FIND-M9-74-V1-SHIMS-RETURN-V2-ENVELOPE was found exactly there: with the save no longer timing out, both comparison tests failed with missing field 'session_a_id'. m7-03 rerouted the deprecated v1 tools through the session_compare dispatcher in 947e73b and silently changed their response shape from the flat v1 result (hand-built json! in the tool body before that commit) to the tagged SessionCompareOutput envelope, while keeping the v1 names, the v1 parameters and the 'DEPRECATED v1 shim ... v1 parameter names are preserved' descriptions. SessionCompareOutput's own doc comment declares the intent the code violated: the shims are supposed to drop provenance so v1 callers see the JSON they saw before m7-03. Nothing pinned it - the four chronos-mcp tests for these tools assert on Debug text that the nested shape also satisfies - and the sandbox client, a v1 client, is the only caller that parses the payload as JSON. A new SessionCompareWire { V2Envelope, V1Flat } parameterises the dispatcher, session_compare keeps the envelope, both shims return the flat CompareSessionsResult / PerformanceRegressionAuditResult, and a new test pins the split by parsing the actual tool payloads. Falsification: reverting put_many to the per-event loop fails test_put_many_commits_once_per_batch (500 barriers for one batch); reverting both shims to V2Envelope fails the new shape test at v["session_a_id"] == null; both reverts restored byte-identically before the green runs. Two T3 anomalies (chronos-e2e test_ptrace_capture hanging, chronos-native lib tests failing and hanging in parallel) were characterised and shown not to involve chronos-store at all; serial runs pass 101/101 and the AGENTS.md 6.5 row was corrected to record the real shape.

findings.summary: Closed as designed by the m9-73 deferral: ContentStore::put_many batches a whole session's events into one redb write transaction, so save_session costs a constant number of durability barriers instead of one fsync per event. The 34,905-event crash session that did not complete in 186 s before now saves inside the 30 s sandbox client timeout, evidenced by session_edge_cases going 4 passed / 2 failed (never completes) -> 6 passed / 0 failed in 65 s with the timeout unchanged.

subject.gap: crates/chronos-store/src/cas.rs::put opened a redb write transaction, ran ensure_table, checked the dedup row, inserted one row and committed; redb's default durability is immediate and set_durability appears nowhere in the crate, so every commit is a sync_data barrier; crates/chronos-store/src/storage.rs::save_session called that in a loop over the session's events. Measured cost: linear at ~4.8 ms/event, i.e. ~168 s for the 34,905 events of the crash session in session_edge_cases, >186 s observed, against a fixed 30 s client timeout in chronos-sandbox and a visible 'session_save takes minutes' problem for any agent saving a realistic session. Everything above ~6,000 events approaches the timeout.
subject.fix: cas.rs: the pure serialize + LZ4 + BLAKE3 step is split into fn encode(event) -> (ContentHash, Vec<u8>) so a batch is encoded before a transaction opens (an encoding failure stores nothing); fn insert_batch(&[(ContentHash, Vec<u8>)]) opens one write transaction, keeps the per-event dedup check (a write transaction reads its own inserts, so intra-batch duplicates collapse as well) and commits once; pub fn put_many(&[TraceEvent]) -> Vec<ContentHash> encodes the whole slice, returns one hash per event in input order and returns early for an empty batch without touching the database; put is now encode + insert_batch with unchanged semantics and hash. storage.rs: save_session calls self.cas.put_many(events) instead of the put loop, documented as CAS-then-metadata ordering whose worst case is unreferenced (but deduplicated and content-addressed) CAS rows. Tests: crates/chronos-store/src/test_support.rs (new, cfg(test)) provides CountingBackend, which wraps redb's real FileBackend and counts sync_data calls, plus counting_file_db; a file-backed store is required because in-memory redb never syncs. cas.rs gains 4 tests (order and per-event hash equality against put, dedup within and across batches with a cas_row_count assertion, empty batch does not create the cas table, 500-event batch <= 3 barriers against a control loop of 50 puts that must issue >= 50) and storage.rs gains 1 (1,000-event save_session <= 4 barriers plus a full round-trip).

evidence.falsification: put_many reverted to the per-event put loop in cas.rs (original kept at /home/rubentxu/.jcode/scratch/cas.rs.m9-74-good): test_put_many_commits_once_per_batch FAILED, with the 500-event batch reporting one barrier per event against the CountingBackend while the 50-put control loop reported >= 50 as required. Restored with cmp byte-identical to the backup and re-ran: cargo test -p chronos-store --lib 74 passed. The acceptance suite supplies the second, independent observation: before the fix the crash-session save did not complete inside 186 s (m9-73, interleaved A/B), after the fix the same test saves a 34,905-event session and proceeds to the comparison step within the 30 s client timeout (suite total 65.1 s).
evidence.post_fix: cargo fmt --all -- --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings clean; cargo test -p chronos-store --lib 74 passed; cargo test -p chronos-mcp --lib 78 passed; T3 workspace minus sandbox minus e2e all green; cargo test -p chronos-native --lib -- --test-threads=1 101 passed; T4-smoke session_edge_cases 6/6 (65.1 s), session_persistence 4/4, multi_session 6/6, e2e_connectivity 1/1, all --test-threads=1 with CHRONOS_MCP_PATH set.

findings.summary: Closed as the observable symptom of the CAS finding, which is now demonstrated rather than inferred: both tests pass with the client timeout untouched at 30 s, and the suite is green 6/6 in 65 s. The two AGENTS.md 6.5 rows for these tests were removed with a note recording where they went.

subject.gap: chronos-sandbox/tests/session_edge_cases.rs::test_compare_sessions_crash_vs_normal and ::test_performance_regression_audit_different_workloads failed on every observed run in this environment (m9-73 measured it on main as well, interleaved A/B, and again with the client timeout raised to 180 s: 186 s and still failing), always at save_session with TimeoutError("method=tools/call", 30s). The suite therefore could not signal regressions in the comparison path at all, and the two failures were pinned in AGENTS.md 6.5 as environmental.
subject.fix: No test change: the cause was the product defect above, and batching the CAS writes makes both tests complete. AGENTS.md 6.5 drops both rows and states that ContentStore::put_many is what closed them, so a future reader does not re-add them as flakes.

evidence.falsification: The claim 'this is the CAS defect, not an environment problem' is falsified by the fix itself: with put_many in place and the client timeout unchanged at 30 s, both previously red tests pass in the same environment that failed them on main and on the m9-73 branch. Conversely the pre-fix behaviour is on record (m9-73: 186 s with a 180 s timeout, on main too), so the two states differ only by this cycle's diff.
evidence.post_fix: cargo test -p chronos-sandbox --test session_edge_cases -- --test-threads=1: 6 passed / 0 failed / 65.10 s (was 4 passed / 2 failed, never completing).

findings.summary: Two deprecated v1 MCP tools stopped honouring their own response contract in m7-03 and nothing noticed because no test parsed their payloads and the only JSON-parsing client could not get that far. Both shims return the flat v1 result again; a new test pins the split between flat shims and the enveloped v2 tool.

subject.gap: m7-03 (947e73b) rerouted compare_sessions and performance_regression_audit through dispatch_session_compare and changed what they return: before that commit the bodies built the flat v1 JSON by hand (session_a_id/session_b_id/only_in_a_count/... and baseline_session_id/target_session_id/...), afterwards they serialize the tagged SessionCompareOutput enum with its provenance. The tool names, the parameter names and the descriptions ('DEPRECATED v1 shim ... the v1 parameter names are preserved') all stayed v1, and SessionCompareOutput's own doc comment states the intended behaviour: 'MCP shims drop the provenance field so existing v1 callers see the same JSON they did before m7-03'. A v1 client therefore receives {kind, result, provenance} where it expects the flat object and fails with missing field 'session_a_id'. Detection was zero: the four chronos-mcp tests for these tools assert on the Debug text of the content and the keys they look for (similarity_pct, common_count, summary) also appear inside the nested envelope, and the sandbox client - the only v1 caller that parses the payload as JSON - was blocked by the save timeout until this cycle.
subject.fix: crates/chronos-mcp/src/server.rs: new enum SessionCompareWire { V2Envelope, V1Flat } with to_value(SessionCompareOutput) that either serializes the envelope or unwraps it to the flat CompareSessionsResult / PerformanceRegressionAuditResult kept in chronos-services::output for this purpose; dispatch_session_compare takes the wire shape as a parameter; session_compare passes V2Envelope and both shims pass V1Flat; both descriptions now state that the v1 response shape is preserved too. New test test_v1_shims_return_flat_result_while_v2_returns_envelope parses the tool content blocks as JSON and asserts that both shims expose session_a_id / baseline_session_id at the top level and leak neither provenance nor result/kind, while session_compare carries kind, provenance and a nested result.session_a_id. Grep confirms these two are the only tools whose description contains 'DEPRECATED v1 shim', so the class is closed.

evidence.falsification: Both shims reverted to SessionCompareWire::V2Envelope: test_v1_shims_return_flat_result_while_v2_returns_envelope FAILED at assert_eq!(v["session_a_id"], json!(sid_a)) - the parsed payload has null where the v1 contract has a string, which is exactly the failure the sandbox client reported as missing field 'session_a_id'. Restored with cmp byte-identical to /home/rubentxu/.jcode/scratch/server.rs.m9-74-good; cargo test -p chronos-mcp --lib 78 passed.
evidence.post_fix: cargo fmt --all -- --check clean; cargo clippy -p chronos-mcp --all-targets -- -D warnings clean; cargo test -p chronos-mcp --lib 78 passed (was 77 before the new test); cargo test -p chronos-sandbox --test session_edge_cases -- --test-threads=1 6 passed / 0 failed, including the two tests that previously failed with missing field 'session_a_id'.

deferred.note: The chronos-native lib suite cannot be run in parallel in this environment: with the default test threads, ptrace_tracer::tests::test_launch_captures_events and ::test_launch_true_and_wait fail, and a third test blocks in waitpid until the harness is killed (observed 17 min at 0% CPU in a futex wait, still blocking after --skip test_launch_with_syscall_tracing). Serially the same suite is 101 passed in 13 s, and test_launch_with_syscall_tracing in isolation is 1 passed in 1.32 s, so it is concurrency between ptrace tests rather than a broken test. Not caused by this cycle - the diff touches chronos-store and chronos-mcp and these tests call PtraceTracer only - and AGENTS.md 6.5 was rewritten in this cycle to record the real shape and the T3 recipe that works here (workspace command for everything except the ptrace crate, plus cargo test -p chronos-native --lib --test-threads=1). The proper remedy is structural: mark the ptrace tests as serial (a test-level lock, a separate test binary, or #[ignore] plus an explicit opt-in target) so that whoever runs the default cargo test does not lose 17 minutes to a silent hang. Not attempted here because it changes test harness structure in a crate this cycle does not otherwise touch.
deferred.severity_rationale: No product impact; the cost is wasted agent/CI time on a silent hang, and it is already documented where the next agent looks.

deferred.note: Unchanged from m9-73 and still open: chronos-mcp::open_default_store falls back to SessionStore::in_memory() when the configured store cannot be opened (locked, corrupt, missing parent), logging only a tracing::warn, so a server asked to open a locked store starts successfully with an empty store, reports session_save success and returns 0 sessions from session_list - silent data loss with a green health check. It is a deliberate resilience choice and the remedy is a policy decision belonging to chronos-mcp (fail closed on a store that exists but cannot be opened, keep the fallback only for a missing parent directory, or surface the degraded mode in the tool response). Detection exists in the sandbox harness (client_store_isolation fails if it ever runs against a fallback store), but nothing fails on the fallback itself in production.
deferred.severity_rationale: Silent data loss, but it needs a store that exists and is locked or unreadable, which in practice means two processes against one configured path.
